title: PRD: Hosted Endpoint Safety Net & Acceptance Kit
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This PRD defines a safety-net and acceptance kit for the hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). Goal: provide a deterministic, testable, and operationally-sane launch path that protects production consumers from regressions and ensures predictable behavior across rollout phases.
background: We have multiple PRDs for endpoint surfaces but inconsistent launch checklists and insufficient rollback triggers. Customers reported subtle behavioral regressions during earlier launches (tokenization differences, truncated outputs, rerank score drift). This initiative bundles a behavioral acceptance kit, telemetry thresholds, canary gating criteria, and an explicit rollback/runbook for endpoint changes.
scope_inclusions: Unified acceptance criteria for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Behavioral regression test harness (prompt/seed set + golden outputs) and automated eval job
Launch checklist with owners for safety checks, monitoring, and rollback criteria
Canary and staged rollout plan; traffic-slicing knobs and telemetry gating
Operational runbooks: rollback procedure, emergency throttles, escalation contacts
scope_exclusions: Deep model architecture changes (model onboarding handled by ModelOps team)
Dedicated/Dedicated Private capacity configuration UI changes
SDK changes beyond surface compatibility shims
requirements: Behavioral spec: define 150 prompts across categories (generation, instruction-following, embeddings similarity, rerank cases) with golden results or metric bounds
Automated eval pipeline that runs nightly and on every canary; outputs pass/fail and diff artifacts
Telemetry SLOs: per-route 95th pct latency, token-cost delta, error-rate thresholds
Canary gating rules that combine automated eval pass, telemetry stability for 30 minutes, and no customer-facing errors > 0.5%
Acceptance checklist items must be owner-assigned and signed off before non-zero traffic ramp
Rollback trigger thresholds (behavioral regression beyond tolerated thresholds or latency/SLA violations) and automated rollback playbook
Documentation: PRD, runbooks, playbook links surfaced in Console and internal runbooks
acceptance_criteria: Automated behavioral eval returns >= 95% pass rate against golden set (or within defined metric bounds) for each endpoint
No increase in client-visible error rate > 0.3% over baseline during a 1h canary window
95th percentile latency <= SLA bound for chosen lane (e.g., chat 95th <= 400ms for minimal lane) during canary
Per-token cost variance < 12% compared to validated baseline under representative traffic profile
Canary traffic slice exercised across at least 3 geographies and 2 tenant classes (free/dev & paid/enterprise)
All checklist items marked complete and owners have acknowledged readiness in comments
Security review completed and signoff recorded for any endpoint changes touching auth/audit flows
launch_checklist: Pre-launch: collect and freeze golden prompt set (owner: Product) and register in eval service
Pre-launch: configure canary slice (owner: Infra) with traffic routing policy and failover path
Pre-launch: baseline telemetry collection for last 7 days for latency, error, cost (owner: Observability)
Pre-launch: QA run of automated eval on staging with full dataset and store diffs (owner: QA)
Golden run: run seq of smoke tests against canary lane (owner: SRE)
Signoffs: Product, Engineering, SRE, Security must comment + approve on ticket (owner: Product)
Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% traffic increments with 30 min stability windows (owner: Release Engineering)
Monitoring: live dashboard for endpoints with alert rules, including behavioral regression alert (owner: Observability)
Backup: ensure immediate rollback route available and tested (owner: SRE)
Post-launch: run full automated eval job at T+1h, T+6h, T+24h and publish results to PRD thread (owner: QA)
Post-launch: 72h hypercare rota assigned with contact list and escalation matrix (owner: Customer Success)
Post-launch: capture customer feedback and compare to pre-launch quality baselines (owner: Product)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 – Staging: end-to-end smoke, automated eval runs, and load stability tests against a synthetic traffic profile
Phase 1 – Canary: route 1% traffic for 30m; if stable and automated eval passes, ramp to 5% for 30m
Phase 2 – Expanded: 20% for 1h across multiple regions and tenant classes; require no critical alerts and behavioral stability
Phase 3 – Majority: 60% for 2h with full logging retention; final signoffs for non-reversible changes
Phase 4 – GA: 100% rollout with extended monitoring and weekly eval comparisons for first month
monitoring_thresholds: Behavioral eval fail rate > 5% triggers critical alert
Customer-visible errors > 0.3% sustained for 15m triggers rollback consideration
95th percentile latency increase > 25% over baseline for 30m triggers investigation
Per-token cost increase > 20% sustained for 1h raises economics rollback discussion
